args.text: When naming BPMN elements, use concise labels that capture the essential action or decision stated in the description; avoid adding subordinate details to a label when they are not necessary to identify the modeled step.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing guideline addresses concise, faithful BPMN labels before proposing a rule for the label divergences.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Declare the BPMN model namespace http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL and a non-empty targetNamespace on bpmn:definitions.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

args.text: When a description lists several attributes or data items handled in one activity, use a concise label naming the essential action rather than enumerating every detail; express decisions with concise questions about the relevant condition.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers concise, focused labels before proposing a refinement.

result.rule: When the description gives an activity together with contextual or explanatory details that are not needed to distinguish the activity in its process context: Label the BPMN task with its core action and necessary object, omitting redundant contextual modifiers while preserving details essential to the activity’s meaning.
When the description specifies multiple distinct actions within one activity: label the BPMN activity so that it communicates each stated action, rather than omitting one
When the description states an occurrence that starts the process: Label the start event with a concise phrase naming that trigger rather than a generic label.
When the description specifies an activity’s object, recipient, or other meaningful qualifier: Preserve that qualifier in the BPMN task label rather than replacing it with a broader paraphrase.

args.text: When the description groups multiple values or attributes under one activity, label the BPMN activity with its core action and object rather than enumerating every value, unless the individual values are needed to distinguish the activity.

trace.reason: Verify that the proposed concise-label guidance applies beyond this process and is not tied to its domain wording.
